name: MCL Two-Anchor Inventory Auction Relay
hypothesis: The first completed CL/MCL auction around Europe and United States liquidity transfer is more causally stable than an all-session boundary: each anchor compares its first joint excursion with only the inventory accumulated before that anchor, then records exactly one next-bar acceptance or failure verdict.

europe.reference: current Globex session through the last completed five-minute bar before 08:00 Europe/London, DST-aware
europe.trigger: first joint CL/MCL close outside that range from 08:05 through 10:00 Europe/London

us.reference: current Globex session through the last completed five-minute bar before 09:00 America/New_York
us.trigger: first joint CL/MCL close outside that range from 09:05 through 10:15 America/New_York

verdict: The immediately next completed five-minute CL/MCL bar must jointly remain outside for acceptance or jointly return inside for failure; disagreement consumes the anchor without a signal.
direction: textbook auction control: acceptance follows the boundary side and failure fades it
execution_projection: exact next one-minute matched-suffix MCL open; count proof records no fill or PnL
frequency_law: maximum one event per anchor and two per Globex session; no quota, second excursion, delayed search, threshold, or missing-event replacement
if_eligible: Freeze one compact lifecycle preregistration before opening any forward return, MFE, MAE, or PnL.
if_ineligible: Reject the two-anchor relay before outcomes; do not widen clocks, reuse an anchor, alter boundaries, add delayed triggers, or lower the cadence floor.
